rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this round pushes reverse-engineering resistance up while guarding the program's dominant cost: loops. SUB gets the highest SecurityGain since arithmetic substitution is cheap, safe, and effective against the heavy constant/template arithmetic in this Adobe-C++ benchmark; IGV and SPLIT are also low-cost structural transforms applied broadly to fragment control flow and data layout across the 175 mostly small functions. FLA and BCF are the expensive transforms on loop-intensive code (loop_invariant, loop_unroll sources), so their RuntimeCost weights are raised to 0.9/0.8 to steer them away from hot loops while keeping SecurityGain moderate so they still apply to cold functions like the 6.7KB main. ICALL and IBR add indirect dispatch and block-randomization with moderate cost sensitivity, providing control-flow diversity without compounding overhead with FLA/BCF. CorrectnessRisk weights stay low (0.1-0.3) across the board since round 0 showed no ICEs, allowing slightly bolder selection without jeopardizing the clean build-and-run record.
